headline: Medium prompt-injection and cascading-error risk from browserless Authelia feeding Marker’s document pipeline; no direct data-leak path is evidenced.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Authelia can ingest and forward-authenticate web content via OAuth/OIDC and ForwardAuth, while Marker is a document-processing agent that may consume external text. No shared channel is documented, so the pathway is inferred rather than observed; uncertainty pushes this above low. The risk is that attacker-controlled document content could be treated as instructions if bridged into Marker’s pipeline.
conditions: IF Authelia forwards untrusted web content into Marker’s input pipeline
IF Marker treats document text as instructions or tool directives without provenance checks
mitigations: Add a provenance banner to all Authelia-fed inputs
Strip instruction-like prefixes from imported documents
Require manual review before Marker processes externally sourced text
Disable any automatic handoff between the two systems
requires-engineering: add content provenance tagging end-to-end

B_data_leakage.rationale: Authelia has broad network egress, but Marker is explicitly network-egress none and read/write filesystem false, so there is no documented path for Marker to exfiltrate data. Both profiles show no data classes touched. The remaining concern is limited to local exposure through any shared workspace, which is not evidenced here and would be small if present.
conditions: IF the operators place sensitive files in a shared workspace
IF Marker is later granted filesystem read or network egress
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Do not mount secrets into Marker’s runtime
Verify Marker remains network-isolated
Review Authelia logs for accidental content capture
requires-engineering: add workspace isolation controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Authelia has broad network egress and OAuth/OIDC-facing APIs, while Marker has no filesystem write, no shell, no subprocesses, and no network egress. Their write surfaces do not overlap in the profiles, so direct resource contention is unlikely. Any conflict would require extra orchestration not shown in either profile, so severity stays low.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator gives both agents write access to the same mutable resource
IF Marker is reconfigured to modify shared state
mitigations: Keep Marker read-only
Avoid shared mutable directories
Separate OAuth/OIDC duties from document processing
Check orchestrator permissions before deployment
requires-engineering: add locking for any shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: Authelia can produce authentication decisions and Marker can process documents, so a plausible chain is Authelia-derived output being consumed by Marker without verification. No evidence shows Marker critically evaluates upstream outputs, and no downstream action authority is documented, so this is not high. Because the interaction is inferred from profiles rather than observed, uncertainty favors medium.
conditions: IF Marker consumes Authelia output as authoritative input
IF no verification step is inserted between authentication output and document processing
mitigations: Insert a validation step before Marker consumes upstream output
Require human review for any derived decisions
Log source provenance alongside each document
Reject malformed or unsigned upstream payloads
requires-engineering: add schema validation between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and docs-only, with no data classes touched and no residency or retention mismatch documented. Authelia’s broad network egress could matter if regulated data were introduced, but that is not shown here. Because the compliance pathway is not evidenced and no specific regulated data flow is present, the risk remains low.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is routed through Authelia into Marker
IF the deployment imposes residency or retention rules not reflected in the profiles
mitigations: Confirm no regulated data enters the pair
Document retention settings for both systems
Keep logs minimal and access-controlled
Review deployment region before go-live
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention
